svg.font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

metadata.orrery:spec: # yaml-language-server: $schema=../references/diagram.schema.json # After Google's Cloud Architecture Center disaster recovery guides and multi-regional deployment # archetype: a global external Application Load Balancer in front of regional managed instance # groups, Cloud SQL high availability across two zones, and a cross-region replica kept warm. title: Multi-region disaster recovery on Google Cloud subtitle: A global load balancer serves us-east1 and fails over to a warm standby in us-west1, whose Cloud SQL replica is promoted direction: down # Product cards, as in Google Cloud's own architecture diagrams; one port per edge. look: card layout: { merge: false } legend: solid: Traffic dashed: Failover path dotted: Database replication groups: gcloud: { type: gcp:cloud } project: { type: gcp:project, label: Project shop-prod, in: gcloud } # One global VPC network holds both regions. vpc: { type: gcp:vpc, label: VPC network, in: project } east: { type: gcp:region, label: us-east1 primary, in: vpc } # The standby's zone comes first, so the replication to us-west1 leaves the primary's # zone on the side facing the other region instead of crossing the standby. east-c: { type: gcp:zone, label: us-east1-c, in: east } east-b: { type: gcp:zone, label: us-east1-b, in: east } west: { type: gcp:region, label: us-west1 standby, in: vpc } west-a: { type: gcp:zone, label: us-west1-a, in: west } # Each regional MIG spans its region's zones, so it sits in the region; the Cloud SQL # instances are zonal and sit in their zones. nodes: users: { icon: generic:users, label: Users } lb: { icon: gcp:cloud-load-balancing, label: Cloud Load Balancing, note: Global external Application LB, in: project } mig-east: { icon: gcp:compute-engine, label: Compute Engine, note: Regional MIG in 2 zones, badge: x4, in: east } # Notes of one length keep the two zones the same width. sql-standby: { icon: gcp:cloud-sql, label: Cloud SQL, note: HA standby, in: east-c } sql-primary: { icon: gcp:cloud-sql, label: Cloud SQL, note: HA primary, in: east-b } mig-west: { icon: gcp:compute-engine, label: Compute Engine, note: Regional MIG scaled down, badge: x2, in: west } sql-replica: { icon: gcp:cloud-sql, label: Cloud SQL, note: Asynchronous read replica, in: west-a } edges: - users -> lb: HTTPS - lb -> mig-east: active backend - lb --> mig-west: failover - mig-east -> sql-primary: private IP - mig-east --> sql-standby: zone failover # Replication links sit side by side in one row; constraint: false keeps them out of the # layout so the zones and the regions stay next to each other. - { from: sql-primary, to: sql-standby, line: dotted, label: sync, constraint: false } - { from: sql-primary, to: sql-replica, line: dotted, constraint: false } - mig-west --> sql-replica: after promotion

svg.title: Multi-region disaster recovery on Google Cloud
svg.desc: Multi-region disaster recovery on Google Cloud. 7 components in 8 groups. Connections: Users to Cloud Load Balancing (HTTPS); Cloud Load Balancing to Compute Engine (active backend); Cloud Load Balancing to Compute Engine (failover); Compute Engine to Cloud SQL (private IP); Compute Engine to Cloud SQL (zone failover); Cloud SQL to Cloud SQL (sync); Cloud SQL to Cloud SQL; Compute Engine to Cloud SQL (after promotion).

text.tspan: MULTI-REGION DISASTER RECOVERY ON GOOGLE CLOUD
A global load balancer serves us-east1 and fails over to a warm standby in us-west1, whose Cloud SQL replica is promoted
